proposal.approach: Recompute the archived optical state from the prior agent lane at both quadrature resolutions.
proposal.what_would_change: Finite quadrature can nominate a violating optical state. A rigorous error bound covering the entire phase plane is required to decide the question.

math_review.hypotheses: The candidate has eight distinct allowed levels and integer amplitudes within range. Its squared coefficient norm is 3204, so dividing by √3204 gives a normalized pure state. In the coherent-amplitude coordinate α = (q + ip)/√2, the Jacobian gives d²α = dq dp/2. With both densities normalized in their respective measures, the proposed inequality becomes Δ = ∫|Wα| d²α − (∫√Qα d²α)²/(4π) ≤ 0. For vacuum the two terms are exactly 1, and displacement preserves both integrals, verifying equality for every coherent state. A single state with Δ > 0 would refute the inequality. A noncoherent state with Δ = 0 would refute the equality characterization.
math_review.weakest_step: The executed coarse and fine grids gave Δ = −0.757329 and −0.757364. I independently evaluated the Fock-state formulas on a 400 × 300 polar midpoint grid over |α| < 10 and obtained 2.113564 − 2.870978 = −0.757414. All three screens put this candidate on the conjectured side, but grid agreement supplies no rigorous error bound. The critical next test for this candidate is to enclose both integrals on the disk using interval bounds and bound their exterior tails using the Gaussian-weighted Fock polynomials. A strictly negative upper bound for Δ would retire this witness rigorously. The universal inequality and the uniqueness of coherent-state equality remain open in this assessment.
